claims.statement: The active workspace has one declared Cargo dependency layer for every workspace package.
claims.falsifier: cargo metadata shows an unassigned package, an upward dependency, a forbidden edge, or a member-local dependency version.

claims.statement: The raw-frame library detects payload tampering and reports incomplete journal tails rather than silently repairing them.
claims.falsifier: a mutated payload passes validation or a torn final record is accepted as a clean journal.

claims.statement: Python experiment records are content-addressable and reject missing pre-registration fields or naive timestamps.
claims.falsifier: the same canonical record receives different hashes, or an invalid record is accepted.

claims.statement: The shared Rust cost model can be called from a JSON-lines research interface without embedding tariff defaults.
claims.falsifier: a missing effective schedule returns zero charges or the app computes fees outside cost-model.

claims.statement: The repository includes a deterministic research-to-paper toolkit, but no strategy is claimed profitable or validated for live trading.
claims.falsifier: A report or README asserts positive alpha/live profitability without licensed point-in-time data, full executable costs, untouched OOS evidence, independent replication and approved controls.

claims.statement: Canonical Upstox/FYERS normalizers preserve vendor timestamp and payload semantics and never infer aggressor side from LTP-only observations.
claims.falsifier: Any normalizer fabricates an exchange sequence, raw packet, confirmed print or aggressor side not supplied by the source.

claims.statement: Point-in-time dataset publication preserves bitemporal listing, corporate-action, universe-membership, event and source-frame lineage and verifies internal artifact integrity.
claims.falsifier: A later-known listing/action is visible to an earlier event, raw prices are mutated, lineage hash sets do not recompute, or an incomplete publication is accepted.

claims.statement: Paper/research OMS and signed permit verifier do not enable live order routing.
claims.falsifier: A feature flag, test signature or verifier result can cause this repository to submit a live broker order without separately approved/certified routing.

claims.statement: The durable OMS commits order intent, an audit event and its outbox command atomically; it never automatically retries a command after dispatch may have begun.
claims.falsifier: The intent can exist without its outbox command after a process crash, an expired DISPATCHING command is automatically resent, or duplicate broker execution IDs are accepted.

claims.statement: Runtime risk evidence is signed only after a root-trusted, fresh, role-scoped set of eight independent signed observations is verified and their source sequences are consumed by a replay ledger.
claims.falsifier: Caller-supplied RiskFacts can be signed through a public API, a tampered/stale/untrusted observation is accepted, or a consumed source sequence can be replayed.

claims.statement: A PIT dataset may be published with a detached Ed25519 signature over a domain-separated canonical manifest digest; verification requires a separately trusted public key and recomputes the artifact and lineage hashes.
claims.falsifier: A signed dataset verifies after manifest/artifact tampering, an unknown signing key is accepted, or source authenticity/completeness is claimed solely from a manifest signature.

claims.statement: The multi-instrument simulator accepts one selected provider stream, models long-only cash reservations across symbols, and never aggregates visible liquidity across provider observations.
claims.falsifier: A mixed-provider replay silently adds displayed depth, an open buy reserve is ignored for another symbol, or a short sale is accepted without inventory.

claims.statement: Release dependency integrity is machine-checked: workflow actions are pinned to commit SHAs, every declared Python dependency is pinned in a resolved constraint set, undocumented advisories fail the audit gate, and the SBOM is generated deterministically from Cargo.lock and the constraint sets.
claims.falsifier: An unpinned `uses:` reference, a declared dependency absent from its constraint file, or an advisory absent from the allowlist passes the gates, or two identical SBOM runs differ.

claims.statement: The versioned exchange reference parsers account for every physical row of a dated source file under a declared version, preserve that outcome on a repeat parse, and fail closed on an undeclared version; compatibility is limited to the tested source versions and categories.
claims.falsifier: A dated source file has a row with no accepted/excluded/rejected outcome, a repeat parse differs from the first, an undeclared format version parses successfully, or a passing run is presented as coverage of untested versions or products.

claims.statement: The shared ingress port preserves original provider bytes and capture metadata for both Upstox raw protobuf frames and FYERS SDK-decoded callback observations, refuses foreign-source or malformed frames, accounts for duplicates and sequence gaps, and replays captured source bytes deterministically into a rebuilt consumer checkpoint after restart without inventing canonical identities.
claims.falsifier: An ingested frame changes its payload bytes or metadata, a foreign-source frame is committed, a duplicate produces a second journal record, a gap or malformed frame is silently ignored, a restart loses the last committed position or payload hash, or an unknown instrument is assigned a canonical identity in the ingress stage.

claims.statement: The fundamental-data validation path rejects malformed company identities and financial facts, validates source-document SHA-256 syntax and evidence locations, validates append-only revisions and derived-fact dependency lineage, and selects only revisions whose publication, observation, ingestion, and required predecessor/input records are known at the requested point in time.
claims.falsifier: A malformed fact or identity is accepted; an invalid document digest or evidence locator passes; a duplicate, broken or cyclic revision/dependency chain passes; a future or unknown-publication fact is selected in a historical as-of view; or the CLI accepts an overlong, aggregate-byte-over-limit, blank, CRLF, BOM-prefixed or torn JSONL record.

claims.statement: A completed FYERS SDK session is imported only after its manifest and full hash chain verify; every record is validated, event and gap metadata survive canonical re-encoding, and repeated imports add no records to the shared raw journal.
claims.falsifier: An invalid manifest or broken chain is imported, a verified record is dropped, gap metadata is lost, or a repeated import adds a second set of journal records.

claims.statement: Canonical projection from Upstox and FYERS verified sources is bound to one exact reference revision and normalizer version, keeps unknown instruments unresolved, requires source-frame hashes, and replays byte-identically in a fresh process.
claims.falsifier: A projection accepts a drifted instrument map, infers an identity for an unknown instrument, omits a source-frame hash when bound, or produces different bytes on a fresh-process replay.

claims.statement: The paper engine consumes a canonical projection only with explicit provider selection, resolved instruments and source-frame lineage; optional reference binding must match the projection, and fresh-process replay is byte-identical.
claims.falsifier: A replay accepts unresolved instruments, unlinked events, a mismatched provider or reference binding, or produces different bytes in a fresh process.

claims.statement: The active SBE decoder reproduces the independent C++ SBE decoder canonical dump for the frozen golden capture byte for byte, re-encodes each message to its exact original bytes, and fails closed on seven malformed inputs.
claims.falsifier: A golden message decodes to a different canonical line, a canonical re-encoding differs from the original bytes, or any of the seven malformed inputs is accepted.

claims.statement: KDB-X analytics is a checked-in, gated repository capability: a typed q contract drives one book per source, its output is pinned by byte-identical golden files and schema-validated digest reports, and a reference check verifies the golden numerically when q is not installed.
claims.falsifier: A q run merges or sums two sources, emits an unknown, missing or duplicated metric, produces different bytes on a fresh process, produces a report that fails its schema, or a golden file that the Rust reference cannot reproduce.

claims.statement: q / kdb+ analytics has the same style-gate treatment as other languages: a canonical style guide with authoritative sources, an added-lines q checker with self-tests wired into make check and CI, and in-process q unit tests over a CSV assertion harness that fail closed on a broken case.
claims.falsifier: A bare / line, unparenthesised count comparison or dotted column access inside a lambda passes the q gate; removing the q checker or its wiring does not fail the style-gate integrity check; or a deliberately failing q assertion exits zero.

claims.statement: All seven source data-rights operations are tri-state with evidence provenance; only PERMITTED authorizes, UNKNOWN/PROHIBITED and undeclared products never do, persistence operations also require a verified entitlement, and the registry instance is schema-validated with format checking. Recorder capture/store and Rust/Python replay boundaries fail closed before creating files or emitting frames. The checked-in registry grants no operation. Local deterministic gates pass; this is implemented, not independently verified, and no commit is claimed here.
claims.falsifier: An UNKNOWN or PROHIBITED right satisfies authorize or evaluate, a recorder creates a journal before Capture and Store are authorized, a replay source emits frames without Replay, a registry instance fails its schema, a negative schema vector passes, a persistence operation succeeds without a verified entitlement, or any right becomes PERMITTED or entitlement.verified true without owner-supplied written evidence.

claims.statement: A newly constructed risk authority denies new risk until session, account snapshot, kill switch and reconciliation readiness are explicitly supplied; control flags do not alter the economic-state revision.
claims.falsifier: A fresh authority accepts a reservation, any default readiness flag is permissive, a control setter changes the revision, or the fresh-authority test does not fail all four checks.

claims.statement: The OMS journal has one exclusive writer and refuses all further mutations after an uncertain append or sync result until an explicit fresh replay; a torn tail fails closed.
claims.falsifier: A second writer can append, a poisoned writer accepts a mutation, a torn tail is accepted on recovery, or a sync failure leaves the writer usable.

claims.statement: Each broker execution is persisted as a typed, independently identifiable event with charge provenance; duplicate delivery is idempotent and malformed events are refused.
claims.falsifier: A fill exists only as cumulative quantity, a duplicate execution id replaces the persisted event or creates a second economic effect, charge status cannot distinguish estimate from confirmation, or an unsupported schema version is accepted.

claims.statement: Every alpha-search result is appended only after a prior registered experiment record claims its holdout; the insert-only registry rejects a second selection claim, tampering, reordering, incomplete trial accounting and holdout leakage, and comparison of two frozen experiments is byte-stable.
claims.falsifier: A search report exists without a registered receipt, two selection claims share one holdout key, a row is updated or deleted successfully, a tampered or non-terminal or leaky record is compared, attempted configs omit losers, or two identical comparisons produce different bytes.

claims.statement: Dataset manifests and rows carry a declarative feature lineage whose as-of time precedes the consuming event and whose knowledge time precedes the as-of time, with a digest that detects edits to the declaration.
claims.falsifier: A future feature definition is accepted for an earlier event, a knowledge time after as-of verifies, an edited feature lineage digest still verifies, or publication succeeds without the lineage block when one was declared.

claims.statement: Opt-in benchmark harnesses emit measured counters and distributions, remain excluded from make check and CI pass/fail gates, and grant no latency or throughput claim.
claims.falsifier: A BENCH-* counter is a hard-coded literal, a benchmark runs as a pass/fail gate in make check or CI, a latency threshold is asserted, or a dated record presents local synthetic numbers as deployment or throughput evidence.

claims.statement: Account projection is deterministic: EventId is derived from (scope, execution_id) with a separate SHA-256 content digest, the exact paise fold and evidenced opening balance are replay-confluent, and busts or charge confirmations resolve the active posting so reversals neither double-apply nor leave residual cash or charges.
claims.falsifier: Two delivery orders of the same fills yield different state digests; a duplicate delivery changes cash or position; a bust after a charge confirmation leaves non-zero cash or negative charges; a second confirmation with a different amount silently no-ops; or an opening without durable evidence is accepted.

claims.statement: Reconciliation classifies duplicate, conflicting, partial, late, out-of-order, unknown-delivery and unavailable cases from independently recomputed OMS and ledger state; every blocking anomaly is reflected in a Mismatch or Unavailable status, and such a report latches reconciliation_blocked until an authenticated operator resolves it.
claims.falsifier: A reused execution id with different content is silently dropped; an unknown delivery is marked blocking but leaves status Matched; a poisoned OMS presents an empty observed view as a match; a latch clears without an authenticated operator resolution; or a fresh intent is reserved while a mismatch or unavailable report is active.

claims.statement: The health decision is made inside RiskAuthority under the reservation mutex over six typed versioned observations from registered producers; unregistered or forged tokens, missing, stale, wrong-version or structurally invalid observations are typed denials, an engaged kill switch persists across restart, and risk-reducing paths remain available when health is degraded.
claims.falsifier: A caller can fabricate all six observations without registering owners, forge another owner's token, pass a safe_for_new_risk boolean or string verdict; a persisted engaged switch is cleared by unauthenticated replay or a release without evidenced reason; or a risk-reducing release/apply_fill is denied by a health condition.

claims.statement: A research job runs only when its manifest validates, its pinned constraint file and code digest match, and its synthetic dataset digest matches; otherwise the runner refuses before execution, and a successful dry-run appends a hash-chained structured run record through the experiment registry.
claims.falsifier: An invalid manifest is accepted; an unpinned or drifted environment passes; a stale dataset hash is not refused; two dry-runs of the same job produce different output digests; or a run completes without an integrity-verifiable registry record.

claims.statement: An independent validation report is deterministic for a frozen record and published dataset, is bounded to internal integrity, and is refused when the record is tampered, its digest is missing or the registry chain is reordered.
claims.falsifier: Two reports for the same frozen record differ in bytes or digest; a tampered record or reordered registry chain still validates; or the report claims data rights, alpha, profitability, entitlement or live readiness.

claims.statement: Published performance evidence records actual measured local synthetic observations with hashes and scope limits; opt-in benchmark lines are never gates and no latency, throughput or readiness claim is made; distribution, allocation, scheduling, licensed data, Fieldbook sharing and target-infrastructure gaps remain owner-gated and unimplemented.
claims.falsifier: A published number is fabricated or a BENCH counter is a hard-coded literal stand-in; a benchmark is added to make check or CI as a gate; a latency threshold is asserted; a dated record presents local synthetic numbers as deployment evidence; or an owner-gated scheduler, allocator, feature store, licensed-data or target-infrastructure gap is silently implemented.

claims.statement: A risk permit is bound to exact order terms by a deterministic SHA-256 digest carried in PermitRef and recomputed in OmsStore::create; a tampered intent, rewritten permit identity or spent permit cannot open an order, while an identical replay is a no-op even after restart.
claims.falsifier: A tampered intent or rewritten policy version/snapshot revision passes create; a permit replayed with a new client id opens a second order; an identical replay creates a second economic effect or consumes a second permit; or a consumed permit is forgotten after recovery. The digest is unkeyed integrity, not a signature: signed permits, KMS keys, production identity and deployed independent risk collectors are explicitly out of scope.

claims.statement: Strategy and synthetic sector exposure are aggregated in exact paise inside the authority mutex, projected once per intent and updated with checked arithmetic across reservation, fill and release; two orders under an order cap but over a strategy cap are denied and a distinct strategy uses its own bucket.
claims.falsifier: Two same-strategy intents summing past the strategy cap are both accepted; a distinct strategy is charged to the first bucket; a release or fill underflows a bucket silently; or an unlabelled instrument passes once a sector cap is configured. A real NSE sector master is external reference data and remains BLOCKED.

claims.statement: Stress, liquidity, Greeks and borrow controls are typed, integer-exact and fail closed on missing synthetic evidence: a configured loss breach, over-participation order, greeks-less derivative and short without borrow or above cost are all denied.
claims.falsifier: A configured parallel shift produces a projected loss past the cap yet is accepted; an order consumes more than the configured fraction of depth or passes with no depth; over-limit or missing derivative greeks pass; or a short with no borrow or above-cost financing passes. Real stress calibration, ADV/depth history, vol/strike surfaces, borrow/funding rates and derivatives expansion remain BLOCKED.

claims.statement: The deterministic recovery drill observes committed prefixes, poisoned writers, a persisted kill switch, a latched reconciliation block and a verified ledger replay at every OMS and account-journal append boundary.
claims.falsifier: A torn OMS or account-journal tail is accepted on recovery, a poisoned writer mutates state, an engaged switch clears across restart, a later Matched reconciliation clears a digest-mismatch latch without authenticated resolution, or the ledger replay fails on the committed prefix. This in-process drill is not independent certification, HA failover, multi-region recovery or certified broker delivery, all of which remain BLOCKED.

claims.statement: The research simulator consumes latency_seed through a declared distribution and records each draw, refuses artifact references that do not resolve to a dated fixture, charges typed borrow/margin/funding terms over logical time, blocks book and trade fills plus new orders during halt, emits one synthetic uncross at a declared price, rounds fills to effective-dated tick size, and recomputes ending cash from committed fills and charges. A local sim-replay driver is byte-stable across hash seeds and the trial store refuses duplicate or conflicting keys. No calibrated, FIFO, real-data, venue-truth, profitability or live-readiness claim is made; the ADR-M1-009 replay-run gate remains a PRECONDITION.
claims.falsifier: Two fresh-process hash seeds yield different verified-equal fields; a fill precedes its sampled activation; a missing or mismatched artifact resolves or a summary says calibrated without a dated calibration result; borrow, margin or funding terms are charged with different typed math; a halt permits a book or trade fill or accepts a new order; a synthetic uncross fills more than once; an effective tick change does not round a later fill; the verifier copies committed ending cash instead of recomputing it; or the trial store overwrites an existing key.

claims.statement: Technical, volatility and statistical features are pure causal functions of synthetic Decimal OHLCV bars, emit timestamped rows bound to a bitemporal FeatureLineage, and produce byte-identical earlier rows after a future extreme bar is appended.
claims.falsifier: An earlier feature value changes when a future bar is appended, a rolling window reads forward, a lineage with knowledge after as-of is accepted, or a changed definition or row digest still verifies.

claims.statement: Momentum and mean-reversion signals are public and byte-identical to the existing screen; factor weights are net-flat and normalize to a declared gross budget; two-leg spread intents are causal; unknown strategy families are refused.
claims.falsifier: A promoted signal differs from alpha_search._signals on the same closes, an appended future bar changes an earlier signal, a factor portfolio leaves its gross budget or is not net-flat, or an undeclared family is accepted.

claims.statement: A registered grid search evaluates only configurations inside the declared search space after a still-open registration, persists every attempted configuration including losers, and appends its terminal record only under the existing complete-accounting and holdout contracts; walk-forward declarations reject split/holdout overlap and missing embargo.
claims.falsifier: An evaluator is called before registration or with an out-of-space config, attempted counts differ from expected_trials or omit losers, a terminal record is appended without a prior registered claim, or a split touching the holdout or lacking embargo passes geometry validation.

claims.statement: Robustness diagnostics use only development observations and declare no final-holdout use; performance, risk and attribution reports carry recomputable digests, reject non-finite inputs and reconcile attribution components to the synthetic total within a declared tolerance.
claims.falsifier: A sign-reversing segment is called stable, a diagnostic that reads holdout indices passes terminal append, a tampered report digest verifies, a non-finite input yields a report, or attribution components fail to reconcile to the declared total.

claims.statement: Universe selection over synthetic membership rows excludes facts first known after as_of_ns and binds the selection with a digest; exact Decimal adjustment factors exist for split and bonus only, with a typed refusal for rights, merger, demerger and demonstration kinds.
claims.falsifier: A membership known after as_of_ns enters the universe, a superseded or invalid membership is selected, an unsupported action returns a finite factor, or a cancelled action changes a price factor.

claims.statement: Simulation namespace modules are direct re-exports of canonical sim objects with no duplicated behavior, and the list-experiments CLI exposes registered and rejected terminal records together with their attempted-config counts.
claims.falsifier: A re-exported symbol is not the identical canonical object, a tampered fill digest still compares equal, rejected records or their attempt counts are omitted from the CLI listing, or a re-export module defines its own engine behavior.

claims.statement: A registered experiment binds bar cadence, timestamp semantics, calendar, annualisation and point-in-time basis before evaluation; a registered search validates ordered timestamps against that cadence and uses only the registered periods_per_year, rejecting conflicting CLI values, bare numeric latency and zero-valued holdout placeholders for unevaluated candidates.
claims.falsifier: A daily registration accepts minute-spaced bars, a minute registration accepts an incompatible interval, a named basis accepts a different period count, a synthetic dataset passes without a synthetic calendar and fixed interval, a CLI value replaces the registered annualisation factor, a bare one-nanosecond latency passes without a declared model, or an unevaluated candidate carries a numeric holdout result.

claims.statement: Registered bar cadence is checked against an expected schedule resolved from a checked-in, digest-verified TEST_FIXTURE calendar artifact rather than one fixed elapsed interval; dataset origin is explicit and manifest-bound, scheduled fixture gaps are accepted, missing scheduled bars fail unless covered by an explicit status, and no absent price is fabricated into a zero or forward-filled observation. Implemented, not real-market verified: no real-market calendar validator, source completeness or profitability claim; fixture provenance cannot certify MARKET origin or exchange-calendar validity.
claims.falsifier: An unknown calendar id or a wrong calendar digest resolves; a config boolean or identifier substring overrides an explicit MARKET origin; a record origin disagrees with its manifest; a bar falls in an auction, break, holiday, weekend or after an early close; a missing session or minute bar inside an active session passes without a status; a status observation carries a numeric price; a five-minute bar passes under the one-minute basis; a CLI value replaces the registered annualisation basis; a fixture calendar marked synthetic:false certifies MARKET origin without EXCHANGE_PUBLISHED, PROVIDER_PUBLISHED or OWNER_VERIFIED provenance; an expected schedule generated from observed first and last timestamps passes a missing first or last bar without independent manifest coverage bounds; or a close-anchored inclusive 09:15-15:30 session yields 376 bars while the registered one-minute basis fixes 375 bars per session and 94500 periods per year without defined bar-open/close schedule math. Implemented, not independently verified; no provider data, rights, completeness, real-market calendar validity or live-readiness claim is made.
